## AI-generated Overview (from reference literature and SuttaCentral)
*This overview was drafted by an AI model from the cited scholarship and SuttaCentral data and may contain errors; verify against the sources before relying on it.*
Bhikkhunī Vibhaṅga Pācittiya 12, entitled *Paṭicchannokāsa* ("Meeting a man in a concealed place"), is an expiation rule for Buddhist nuns (*bhikkhunīs*) in the Vinaya Piṭaka [SuttaCentral]. The rule stipulates that a nun who, seeking privacy, stands alone with a man in a concealed place incurs an offense requiring confession (*pācittiya*) [SuttaCentral]. In her study of the nuns' legal corpus, Ute Hüsken analyzes Pācittiya 12 as part of a closely related cluster of rules (including Pācittiyas 11, 13, and 14) that regulate standing or conversing with a man in private or compromised locations [Hüsken 1997]. Hüsken notes that entering a concealed place functions as a preparatory act related to Pārājika 4 (where it constitutes a grave offense, *thullaccaya*), culminating in a *pācittiya* when a nun engages in conversation with a man there [Hüsken 1997]. She further observes an asymmetry with corresponding monks' rules, where standing is often exempted in circumstances where sitting together in seclusion is prohibited [Hüsken 1997].
Curated parallels recorded on SuttaCentral demonstrate that this precept is shared across major Vinaya lineages, including the Dharmaguptaka (Bi Vb Pc 81), Mahīśāsaka (Bi Vb Pc 78), Sarvāstivāda (Bi Vb Pc 83), and Mūlasarvāstivāda traditions in both Chinese (Pc 83) and Tibetan (Pc 100), as well as their corresponding prātimokṣa codes and the Pali *Bhikkhunī Parivāra* [SuttaCentral]. Computational analysis via DharmaNexus corroborates this cross-tradition transmission, recording matches with Sanskrit *Bhikṣuṇīvinaya* texts and Tibetan *Vinayavibhaṅga* recensions [DharmaNexus]. Internally within the Pali canon, DharmaNexus detects extensive shared phrasing between Pācittiya 12 and adjacent monastic rules in the *Bhikkhunī Vibhaṅga* (notably Pācittiyas 11, 13, and 14, and Saṅghādisesa 3), as well as subcommentarial citations in the *Vinayavinicchayaṭīkā* [DharmaNexus].
